text:
maria: heads-up — noticed a spike in quota burn for a bunch of small customers right after the latest py-sdk release. dashboards show batch_size pops for many short requests.
jonathan: oof, was that the PR that enabled dynamic batching by default? iirc we only tested it on long-sequence workloads. link: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/1429
alex: confirming — SRE saw simultaneous increases in token/second across dev and staging at 09:03 UTC. one tenant hit quota alert.
maria: i rolled a quick grep, payloads are 1-20 tokens but batch_size went up to 64, so more tokens billed than expected.
johnathan: (typo) jonathan: meant to say dynamic batching + prefix coalescing. default heuristic changed when no explicit batch config is set. it's in the SDK runtime config: `enable_dynamic_batching=True`
rachel: yikes. SDK release notes should have called this out. users who rely on per-request small calls will see cost regressions.
sre-ops: quota-bot triggered console alert: "Tenant xyz exceeded 95% of monthly token quota in 2h" — correlates with py-sdk 1.8.0 rollout.
maria: is there a quick rollback option? can we flip a server-side flag to respect legacy batching? or release patch?
jonathan: we can ship a 1.8.1 that defaults `enable_dynamic_batching=False` and mark it a bugfix. also push a server-side compatibility gate that honors the explicit `batching` header if present.
alex: server-side gate helps but console dashboards are already misattributing cost to wrong usage buckets because the telemetry header used for route/tenant attribution isn't present on merged-batches. we need to preserve and merge headers during batching.
rachel: exactly — the console shows tokens billed to `internal:proxy` instead of tenant cost centers. that's why support tickets are blowing up.
maria: sample of problematic header drop in logs:
```
Request 12345 headers: x-route: tenant/abc
Batched request id: 54321 headers: x-route: internal:proxy
```
jonathan: that's a bug — batched aggregator should aggregate per-request route headers and preserve tenant-level attribution. i'll open an infra ticket.
sre-ops: short-term mitigation: can we detect tiny payload patterns and opt-out of dynamic batching for <=32 tokens? cheap hack.
jonathan: yes, add a guard clause in the SDK runtime and server router for now. will also add unit tests to cover header propagation in batch merges.
rachel: communication plan: we should post in #announcements and update release notes + migration guide. include cost impact guidance and how to pin behavior.
maria: agreed. i'll prepare a concise Slack blurb and a support playbook for customers who already saw spikes.
jonathan: plan of action: 1) hotfix 1.8.1 with default off + tests 2) server-side gate for legacy behavior 3) header merge fix 4) dashboard reconciliation job to reattribute costs for affected window 5) announcement + support template.
alex: FYI — reattr job likely needs billing team signoff, may take 48-72h. queueing a billing ticket.
sre-ops: deploying a temporary rate-limiter to slow suspected flooders, will throttle non-verified tenants until patch lands. :lock:
devex-bot: deploy queued: py-sdk/1.8.1-hotfix -> blue Canary (initiated by jonathan)
maria: thanks all. keeping this thread updated. retrospective after billing reconcile. :coffee: 
sre-ops: logging note: add histogram metric `sdk.dynamic_batch_multiplier` with percentiles so we can alert before quotas burn next time.
jonathan: will add telemetry + a console tile for it in the short term.
rachel: also add a short example in the docs showing how to force `batching={"enabled":false}` per-client for sensitive workflows.
maria: any blockers?
jonathan: none from eng side, starting patch now.
alex: i'll chase billing and start the reattr request.
maria: rolling this into the postmortem: root cause = aggressive default in SDK + missing header merge. action items assigned.
